page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.4xlarge is a storage- and memory-focused virtual machine instance within the Local SSDs family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 threads powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The architecture incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction support including AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), AES-NI, and BMI2. The instance includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

A key differentiator of this instance configuration is its integrated storage subsystem, featuring 3839 GB of local SSD storage directly bundled with the machine. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The instance contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reveal average multi-core compute and memory metrics, recording 14014.69 on stress-ng multi-core and 7286.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Single-threaded throughput leans weaker in comparison, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1314.68 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 22.9 GB/sec.

Memory throughput reaches 88.96 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 48.96 GB/sec on large-block writes, while cached small-block reads reach 781.6 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks show solid transactional capacity, highlighted by 13.67 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a PassMark database score of 5625.65. While high-parameter LLM inference is limited by single-thread constraints and absence of GPUs, small 135M model generation processes at 182.04 tokens per second.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the inclusion of direct-attached NVMe-class local SSD capacity alongside high memory density eliminates secondary network-attached block storage overheads for data-heavy configurations. The system is well configured for IO-intensive transactional databases, distributed key-value caches like Redis, big data processing, and search index nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.4xlarge is a local storage and memory-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores), 128.0 GB of memory, and 3839 GB of integrated local SSD storage, backed by 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The system architecture supports AVX-512 extensions and registers balanced multi-threaded compute, scoring 14014.69 on stress-ng multi-core and 7286.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth reaches 88.96 GB/sec for large uncached reads, supporting high transactional rates such as 13.67 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. While single-thread instruction throughput represents an architectural tradeoff, the combination of high RAM capacity and large direct-attached solid-state storage makes this server practical for operational databases, caching layers, and search engines requiring fast local I/O.
